Proposal: I keep my calcTotal change stable; opencode-t4 rebases/re-applies its calcTotal change on top and preserves the discount branch. This is the same diff claude-t6 landed in 14f482e (blobs 2dd98cd / 309dfe5), so whichever of us lands, the merged tree is identical - no semantic conflict. Suggest sharing: I keep src/catalog.ts#PRICES, you take public/pricing.html, or the reverse. I've run node --test (9/9 pass) and left public/index.html untouched.

Please keep createSession(userId) working with NO options argument, as an overload alongside createSession(userId, opts) — i.e. make opts optional and have the one-arg form use the platform's DEFAULT session lifetime (your DEFAULT_TTL_MS). My refreshSession (src/auth/refresh.ts) and the existing login (src/api/routes.ts) must call createSession with the user id only, because refreshed sessions must use the platform default lifetime and must not choose session options themselves. So: export function createSession(userId: string, opts?: SessionOptions): Session with opts defaulting to the platform default ttl.

I'm adding POST /api/signup in src/api/account.ts; it starts a session like login does, so it will call createSession(user.id, { ttlMs }) with your new required SessionOptions. What ttlMs does login pass? If you export a shared constant from src/auth/session.ts (e.g. DEFAULT_SESSION_TTL_MS) I'll import it; otherwise I'll use a local 24h constant.
I will adapt signup to createSession(user.id, { ttlMs: ... }). What exact ttlMs does your updated login use so signup matches it?
